record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometric Methods for Instance-Based Learning
record.original_question: Is there a condensing algorithm for instance-based learning that works well both when the data distributions are homogeneous and when they are not, rather than performing well in only one of those situations?

evidence.quote: Therefore a challenging open problem is to find an algorithm that works well in all situations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. In instance-based (nearest-neighbor type) classification, a training set $T = \{(x_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^n \subset \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{Y}$ is used directly at prediction time: a query $x \in \mathcal{X}$ is classified using the labels of its nearest neighbors in $T$ under a metric $d$ on $\mathcal{X}$. A condensing algorithm is a procedure $\mathcal{A}$ that outputs a subset (or, more generally, a set of prototypes) $S = \mathcal{A}(T)$ with $|S| \ll |T|$, intended to be used in place of $T$ for nearest-neighbor classification.

Call a labeled training set homogeneous if the class-conditional distributions are well separated and class regions form compact connected clusters with low overlap; call it non-homogeneous otherwise (e.g., classes with overlapping supports, multimodal class regions, varying local density, or high boundary complexity).

For a condensing algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ and a data distribution $\mathcal{D}$ on $\mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{Y}$, define its performance to consist of (i) the reduction ratio $|S|/|T|$ and (ii) the generalization accuracy of the nearest-neighbor classifier built on $S = \mathcal{A}(T)$, measured against $\mathcal{D}$.

Problem. Does there exist a single condensing algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ that simultaneously achieves high reduction ratio and high generalization accuracy in both the homogeneous and the non-homogeneous regimes, rather than performing well only in one of the two regimes? Equivalently, exhibit such an algorithm together with theoretical or empirical guarantees over both regimes, or prove that no condensing algorithm can be uniformly competitive across both regimes.
artifact.status_search_result: Research on prototype selection and generation (e.g., RHC, RSP3, and multi-label extensions like MLRHC) continues actively, with different algorithms favoring either homogeneous or heterogeneous class structures. No authoritative source confirms the existence of a single condensing algorithm that uniformly dominates across both regimes, nor a proof of impossibility, so the status remains unverified.

status_evidence.title: Data reduction via multi-label prototype generation
status_evidence.snippet: RHC and RSP3 are parameter-free prototype generation algorithms based on identifying homogeneous clusters; extensions such as MLRHC adapt the notion of homogeneity to multi-label data.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on condensing/prototype-generation algorithms, with methods specialized to particular data-structure assumptions.

status_evidence.title: Instance-based learning algorithms
status_evidence.snippet: Instance-based learning algorithms reduce storage by selecting representative training instances; performance varies with data distribution characteristics.
status_evidence.claim: Existing condensing schemes exhibit sensitivity to underlying data-distribution homogeneity.
